headline.hi: Board Exam Ke Liye Must-Do Questions!
headline.en: Must-Do Questions for the Board Exam!

subtext.hi: Wo questions jo har saal CBSE board exams mein repeat hote hain — objective aur subjective dono.
subtext.en: Questions that repeat every year in CBSE board exams — both objective and subjective.

text.hi: CBSE Class 10 board exam mein Trigonometry se total ~8-12 marks aate hain — aur ye ek scoring chapter hai! Agar table aur teeno identities yaad hain, toh full marks pakke. Is lesson mein wahi questions hain jo har saal repeat hote hain.
text.en: Trigonometry carries about 8-12 marks in the CBSE Class 10 board exam — and it's a scoring chapter! If you know the table and the three identities, full marks are guaranteed. This lesson covers the questions that repeat every year.

content.hi: Marks distribution: 1-mark questions — values find karna (standard angles); 2-mark — ratios nikaalna ya simple prove karna; 3-mark — identities prove karna; 4-mark — complex proof ya application. Table yaad honi chahiye — bina iske kuch nahi hoga!
content.en: Marks distribution: 1-mark questions — finding values (standard angles); 2-mark — finding ratios or simple proofs; 3-mark — proving identities; 4-mark — complex proofs or applications. You must know the table — nothing works without it!

content.hi: Objective questions mein time bachane ke liye table aur identities directly use karo, poora derivation likhne ki zaroorat nahi. Subjective (proof) questions mein step-by-step LHS ko RHS ke barabar lao — beech ke steps bhi marks dete hain.
content.en: For objective questions, save time by directly using the table and identities — no need to write the full derivation. For subjective (proof) questions, bring LHS to RHS step-by-step — intermediate steps also earn marks.

caption.hi: Pattern same rehta hai, sirf numbers change hote hain — isliye practice karne se confidence sabse zyada badhta hai.
caption.en: The pattern stays the same, only the numbers change — that's why practice builds confidence the most.

problem.hi: Evaluate karo: (5 cos² 60° + 4 sec² 30° − tan² 45°) / (sin² 30° + cos² 30°)
Prove karo: (cosec θ − cot θ)² = (1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ)
problem.en: Prove that: (cosec θ − cot θ)² = (1 − cos θ) / (1 + cos θ)

steps.hi: LHS = (1/sin θ − cos θ/sin θ)² = [(1−cos θ)/sin θ]²
steps.en: LHS = (1/sin θ − cos θ/sin θ)² = [(1−cos θ)/sin θ]²

steps.hi: = (1−cos θ)²/[(1−cos θ)(1+cos θ)] = (1−cos θ)/(1+cos θ) = RHS ✓
steps.en: = (1−cos θ)²/[(1−cos θ)(1+cos θ)] = (1−cos θ)/(1+cos θ) = RHS ✓

problem.hi: Agar tan θ + cot θ = 2 hai, toh tan²θ + cot²θ nikaalo.
problem.en: If tan θ + cot θ = 2, find tan²θ + cot²θ.

steps.hi: (a+b)² = a²+b²+2ab, isliye tan²θ+cot²θ = (tan θ+cot θ)² − 2·tan θ·cot θ
steps.en: (a+b)² = a²+b²+2ab, so tan²θ+cot²θ = (tan θ+cot θ)² − 2·tan θ·cot θ

problem.hi: Agar sin θ = (a²−b²)/(a²+b²) hai, toh cos θ aur tan θ nikaalo.
problem.en: If sin θ = (a²−b²)/(a²+b²), find cos θ and tan θ.

steps.hi: cos θ = B/H = 2ab/(a²+b²),  tan θ = P/B = (a²−b²)/2ab
steps.en: cos θ = B/H = 2ab/(a²+b²),  tan θ = P/B = (a²−b²)/2ab

question.hi: Agar tan A = 5/12 hai, toh sin A = ?
question.en: If tan A = 5/12, then sin A = ?

explanation.hi: Sahi — ye Identity (2) hai, cos²θ se divide karke sin²θ+cos²θ=1 se derive hoti hai.
explanation.en: True — this is Identity (2), derived by dividing sin²θ+cos²θ=1 by cos²θ.

explanation.hi: 2(1)²+ (√3/2)²−(√3/2)² = 2+0 = 2 (cos²30° aur sin²60° dono 3/4 hain, cancel ho jaate hain)
explanation.en: 2(1)²+(√3/2)²−(√3/2)² = 2+0 = 2 (cos²30° and sin²60° are both 3/4, they cancel)

question.hi: Agar sin θ + cos θ = √2 hai, toh sin θ cos θ = ?
question.en: If sin θ + cos θ = √2, then sin θ cos θ = ?

explanation.hi: Square karo: 1+2sinθcosθ=2 → sinθcosθ=1/2. (√2 hi is equation ka maximum possible value hai, θ=45° par).
explanation.en: Square it: 1+2sinθcosθ=2 → sinθcosθ=1/2. (√2 is exactly the maximum possible value here, achieved at θ=45°.)

explanation.hi: 1×1×0 = 0 (tan 0°=0 hone ki wajah se poora product 0 ho jaata hai)

question.hi: Identity prove karne ki sabse best strategy kya hai?
question.en: What is the best strategy for proving an identity?

options.hi: LHS ko simplify karke RHS ke barabar lao

explanation.hi: Standard strategy: complex side (usually LHS) ko step-by-step simplify karo jab tak simple side (RHS) na mile.
explanation.en: Standard strategy: simplify the more complex side (usually LHS) step-by-step until it matches the simpler side (RHS).
